speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, everyone.
zh: 嘿，大家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Arjun Singh.
zh: 我是 Arjun Singh。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today I'm going to talk to you about multiplayer agentic engineering, or how to enable your whole team and your best agents to work together.
zh: 今天我要和你们谈论多人智能体工程，或者说是如何让你们的整个团队和你们最好的智能体一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go to the talks or go around the expo, you're going to see that a lot of people are talking about putting the agents at the center of everything.
zh: 如果你去听讲座或者在展会转转，你会看到很多人在谈论把智能体置于一切的中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes sense.
zh: 这有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're really powerful.
zh: 它们真的很强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're really cool.
zh: 它们真的很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you don't see a lot of people talking about the people, like this is all for us to make us, our lives better or more productive or whatever.
zh: 但你没看到太多人在谈论人，像这都是为了让我们，我们的生活更好或更高效或诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're going to really focus on how the people fit into these agentic workflows.
zh: 所以我们将真正专注于人如何融入这些智能体工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just a little bit about us first.
zh: 首先简单介绍一下我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our team has worked together building software for over a decade.
zh: 所以我们的团队一起构建软件已经超过十年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: My co-founder, Sergey, and I, we met in the PhD program at Berkeley.
zh: 我的联合创始人 Sergey 和我，我们在 Berkeley 的博士项目中相遇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked on robotics.
zh: 我研究机器人技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: He worked on computer vision.
zh: 他研究计算机视觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And during that, we co-founded a company called Gradescope.
zh: 在此期间，我们联合创办了一家名为 Gradescope 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of you may have used it.
zh: 你们中有些人可能用过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's used by millions of students worldwide at thousands of universities, helped instructors grade their students' work.
zh: 它被全世界数以百万计的学生在数千所大学中使用，帮助讲师给学生的作业打分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And pretty much the entire team working on Superconductor used to work together on Gradescope.
zh: 几乎整个在 Superconductor 工作的团队过去都一起在 Gradescope 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've had a team that's worked together productively from first user to acquisition, working on something new together again.
zh: 所以我们有一个从第一个用户到被收购一直富有成效地一起工作的团队，现在又在一起做一些新的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's kind of an interesting experiment because over the past year we've very aggressively integrated agents in our workflows and we've kind of surfaced all the different bottlenecks and friction points that come up and how to do that productively and keep collaborating the way we used to but with the new power of agents.
zh: 我认为这有点像一个有趣的实验，因为在过去的一年里我们非常积极地将智能体整合到我们的工作流中，我们有点摸清了所有出现的不同瓶颈和摩擦点，以及如何富有成效地做到这一点，并像以前那样继续协作，但拥有智能体的新力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So today I'm gonna talk to you about how, you know, the lessons we learned from kind of solving those friction points and solving those bottlenecks.
zh: 所以今天我要和你们谈论，你知道，我们从解决那些摩擦点和瓶颈中学到的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the talk description I mentioned five lessons and I'm gonna be an engineer and start from zero and add a sixth one in there.
zh: 在讲座描述中我提到了五个教训，我要做一个工程师从零开始，在那里加上第六个。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one I'm gonna start with is just to be model and harness agnostic.
zh: 我要讲的第一个就是，做模型和 harness 不可知论者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a few reasons for that.
zh: 这有几个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best model and harness can change weekly.
zh: 最好的模型和 harness 每周都会变。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could change because a new one comes out.
zh: 变化可能是因为出了一个新模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could change because the best one got taken away.
zh: 变化可能是因为最好的那个被拿走了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things happen and you don't want that to disrupt your entire team's flow.
zh: 事情会发生，你不想因此破坏你整个团队的工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing is that open weight models are actually pretty good now.
zh: 另一件事是，开源权重的模型现在实际上相当好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been really happy with GLM 5.2.
zh: 我们对 GLM 5.2 非常满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're much cheaper, and you want to be able to kind of explore with them and integrate them without, again, having to change the entire workflow.
zh: 它们便宜得多，你希望能够在不必再次改变整个工作流的情况下探索它们并整合它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: The last thing I'll mention on this is that the incentives of the people selling you tokens aren't really aligned with yours.
zh: 关于这点我要提到的最后一件事是，卖给你 token 的人的激励措施与你的并不真正一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're here for a reason, so you're working on things for a reason, you're trying to make your customers' lives better, make your product better, delight your customers, and they want to sell you more tokens.
zh: 你在这里是有原因的，所以你做事情是有原因的，你试图让你的客户的生活更好，让你的产品更好，让你的客户高兴，而他们想卖给你更多的 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you might be happy to pay for as many tokens as it takes, but you don't want to pay for more than that.
zh: 你可能愿意支付所需的尽可能多的 token，但你不想支付比那更多的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, again, kind of being able to switch between things lets you stay in control of all of that.
zh: 所以，再次，能够在不同事物之间切换让你能掌控这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as I go through the talk, I'll mention a couple of places where our product makes it easy for us.
zh: 所以当我在讲座中继续时，我会提到几个我们的产品让我们很容易做到这一点的方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: But whether you use us or not, I'm just going to leave things with you that I think are really important for you to be able to work collaboratively effectively.
zh: 但无论你是否使用我们，我只是要留下一些我认为对你能够有效协作非常重要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the next one is to turn every human interface into an agent and human interface.
zh: 所以下一个是把每个接口都变成智能体和人接口。

speaker: Unknown
en: So typically when people are working with coding agents, they're on their laptop, kind of stuck on that laptop.
zh: 所以通常当人们与编码智能体一起工作时，他们在他们的笔记本电脑上，有点被困在那台笔记本电脑上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody else can talk to that agent.
zh: 没有其他人能与那个智能体对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first place people go to kind of expose more interfaces for them is Slack.
zh: 所以人们去做的第一个地方是为他们暴露更多接口的是 Slack。

speaker: Unknown
en: Claude has a Slack bot, Codex has a Slack bot, we have a Slack bot.
zh: Claude 有一个 Slack 机器人，Codex 有一个 Slack 机器人，我们有一个 Slack 机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really cool.
zh: 这真的很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can say add superconductor, do x, y, z, it does it, somebody else can talk to it.
zh: 你可以说添加 superconductor，做 x, y, z，它就做了，其他人可以与它对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's not enough, because now we've taken it from trapped on somebody's laptop to kind of trapped in Slack.
zh: 但这还不够，因为现在我们已经把它从被困在某个人的笔记本电脑上变成了被困在 Slack 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of work happens in Slack, so that's better than nothing, but certainly not all work happens in Slack.
zh: 很多工作发生在 Slack 里，所以这比没有好，但当然不是所有工作都发生在 Slack 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we really wanted was to be able to work with the same session from every relevant interface.
zh: 所以我们真正想要的是能够从每个相关接口使用同一个会话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could be Slack, could be our app, could be GitHub, could be elsewhere.
zh: 可能是 Slack，可能是我们的应用，可能是 GitHub，可能是其他地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one possible flow is you start and collaborate on a session in Slack, and then maybe you continue in a kind of more engineer-focused environment in the desktop app or the mobile app.
zh: 所以一个可能的工作流是你在 Slack 开始并协作一个会话，然后也许你在桌面应用或移动应用中更专注于工程师的环境中继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can finish it up in GitHub.
zh: 然后你可以在 GitHub 里把它完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the important thing here is it's the exact same agent session, so it's like the agent didn't forget what you did in one place in Slack when you go and talk to it from GitHub.
zh: 这里重要的一点是，这是完全相同的智能体会话，所以就像智能体没有忘记你在 Slack 一个地方所做的事情，当你去 GitHub 跟它对话时。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the same session, it's got the same context.
zh: 它是同一个会话，它拥有相同的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second lesson builds on top of that, which is to make the agent work visible and collaborative across the team.
zh: 第二个教训在此基础上建立，即让智能体的工作在团队中可见且协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so obviously Slack makes it more collaborative.
zh: 很明显，Slack 让它更具协作性。

speaker: Unknown
en: But here, we've got that kind of app view.
zh: 但在这里，我们有那种应用程序视图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Sergey made this ticket.
zh: Sergey 创建了这个工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been talking to the same ticket.
zh: 我一直在跟同一个工单对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: A growth person hopped in as well.
zh: 一个增长人员也跳进来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can kind of see at the top here all the different people that interacted with it.
zh: 所以你可以在顶部看到所有与之互动过的不同人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I can see who's gonna notify about this session, who's seen it.
zh: 所以我可以看到谁会收到关于这个会话的通知，谁看过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's especially important when you have work triggered by non-technical people.
zh: 当你有非技术人员触发的工作时，这尤其重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like our customer support person created a ticket.
zh: 就像我们的客户支持人员创建了一个工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's working really well.
zh: 它运作得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to understand has this been vetted by an engineer or not and kind of see who's involved really easily.
zh: 我想了解这是否已经过工程师的审查，以及能很容易地看到谁参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if I'm reviewing something, I can just pop in and say, like, hey, why did you do it this way?
zh: 然后如果我在审查某样东西，我可以跳进去说，嘿，你为什么这样做？

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, because it's the same agent session, I don't need to wait for Sergey to kind of get my notification on GitHub and respond to me.
zh: 同样，因为它是同一个智能体会话，我不需要等 Sergey 在 GitHub 上收到我的通知并回复我。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer to the question's almost certainly in this thread.
zh: 问题的答案几乎肯定就在这个线程里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also don't want to read the entire thread, so I can just ask the agent.
zh: 我也不想读整个线程，所以我可以直接问智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or how we most often kind of make the work visible is with artifacts.
zh: 或者我们要常让工作可见的方式，是用 artifacts。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it doesn't matter where the work started or where it's finishing.
zh: 所以工作在哪里开始或在哪里结束并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The agent can show you the work it's doing as a screenshot or a video or other, and you can see it from everywhere.
zh: 智能体可以向你展示它正在做的工作，作为截图或视频或其他，你可以从任何地方看到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, you don't have to worry about like, where is that thing?
zh: 所以同样，你不必担心像，那个东西在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: I gotta go to GitHub to see the image, or I gotta go to Slack to see the image.
zh: 我得去 GitHub 看那个图片，或者我得去 Slack 看那个图片。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just everywhere.
zh: 它就在任何地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Work is visible everywhere.
zh: 工作在任何地方都可见。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can collaborate from anywhere.
zh: 你可以从任何地方协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third lesson I'm gonna talk about here is to turn every external signal into code that your team can quickly evaluate.
zh: 我要在这里谈论的第三个教训是，将每个外部信号转化为你的团队可以快速评估的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was hoping to show this live, but the Wi-Fi is not quite there, so I'm gonna show you something from yesterday.
zh: 我本希望能现场演示这个，但 Wi-Fi 有点不行，所以我给你们看昨天的一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what do I mean by external signal?
zh: 但我所说的外部信号是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it could be Slack conversation.
zh: 所以它可能是 Slack 对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be a meeting you have with a customer, an onboarding call, a sales call.
zh: 它可能是你与客户的会议，入职通话，销售通话。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be an internal team meeting.
zh: 它可能是内部团队会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be something from Sentry or a bug tracker, a bug report from a customer, an email feature request.
zh: 它可能来自 Sentry 或错误追踪器，客户的错误报告，电子邮件功能请求。

speaker: Unknown
en: And right now what's happening is all that stuff already exists.
zh: 现在正在发生的是，所有这些东西已经存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's in all those different systems.
zh: 它们在所有那些不同的系统中。

speaker: Unknown
en: People hook them together with MCPs, so now your coding agent can check the email or check Notion or whatever it might be, but how does it know what to work on?
zh: 人们用 MCP 将它们连接起来，所以现在你的编码智能体可以检查电子邮件或检查 Notion 或任何它可能的东西，但它怎么知道要做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still kind of stuck everywhere.
zh: 它还是有点到处卡住。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so some humans are involved in taking stuff from one place and telling it, solve email number 48 or ticket number 6,000.
zh: 所以有一些人参与从一处拿东西并告诉它，解决电子邮件编号 48 或工单编号 6000。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's still a lot of coordination.
zh: 那还是很多协调工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we do is we have several different ways to automatically ingest these signals, prioritize what to do with it, and kind of act on them.
zh: 我们所做的是，我们有几种不同的方式来自动摄取这些信号，确定优先级处理，并对其采取行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my favorite one, the most fun one, is what we call our meeting bot.
zh: 我最喜欢的一个，也是最有意思的一个，是我们所谓的会议机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm going to switch over to my browser here for a second.
zh: 所以我要在这里切换到我的浏览器一秒钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've got a booth at the expo, and we had the meeting bot running all day yesterday.
zh: 我们在展会上有一个展位，我们昨天让会议机器人运行了一整天。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a four-hour meeting of a Google Meet.
zh: 所以这是一个 Google Meet 的四小时会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just kind of invite the bot to meet or Zoom or Teams or whatever it might be.
zh: 你只需邀请机器人去 Meet 或 Zoom 或 Teams 或任何它可能的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it listens all day.
zh: 它会听一整天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it created all sorts of stuff as it was listening.
zh: 它在听的时候创建了各种各样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it finds existing work, it'll link to it.
zh: 如果它发现现有的工作，它会链接到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not gonna just create new work if it's something you're already working on.
zh: 所以如果它已经是你正在做的事情，它不会只创建新的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of this is people testing the meeting bot out and telling it to do some weird things or interesting things or just creative ideas.
zh: 其中有些是人们测试会议机器人并告诉它做一些奇怪的事情或有趣的事情或者只是有创意的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But a lot of it's actually just really good ideas that come out of people looking at what we're doing, asking questions, having new ideas of what to do with it.
zh: 但其中很多实际上确实是好主意,来自于人们关注我们在做什么、提出问题,以及关于用它做什么的新想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's kind of nice, because the last idea that was here was saying, hey, when I work with coding agents, I want to make sure that the agent has clear criteria to evaluate whether it did a good job on the work before it tells me that it's done.
zh: 所以这很不错,因为这里的最后一个想法是说,嘿,当我与编码智能体一起工作时,我想确保智能体有明确的标准来评估它在告诉我它完成之前是否做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they had that idea.
zh: 于是他们有了那个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bot just picked up on it.
zh: 机器人只是注意到了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: None of us did anything manually.
zh: 我们没有人手动做任何事。

speaker: Unknown
en: They created this ticket and started working on it.
zh: 他们创建了这个工单并开始处理它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I was able to just say, hey, take a screenshot of what you did.
zh: 然后我就能够直接说,嘿,把你做的事截个图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's that screenshot.
zh: 这就是那个截图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it kind of modified our ticket form to add these two new fields of acceptance criteria.
zh: 它某种程度上修改了我们的工单表单,添加了这两个新的验收标准字段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, am I going to ship this one exactly how it is?
zh: 现在,我会原样发布这个吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, probably not.
zh: 不,大概不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's a new idea.
zh: 但这是一个新想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's concrete.
zh: 它是具体的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can play with it.
zh: 我可以摆弄它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can go and actually use the live preview and see if this improves performance.
zh: 我可以去实际使用实时预览,看看这是否提高了性能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it takes your hundreds or thousands of ideas that are everywhere and helps you kind of move with the speed of what your customers are asking you for and what they're thinking.
zh: 因此它获取了你到处都有的数百或数千个想法,并帮助你某种程度上以你的客户所要求和思考的速度前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really fun because every time we have an onboarding or customer call or team meeting, we almost always have dozens of new ideas that are prototyped, but more importantly, at least a few shippable PRs with very minimal intervention.
zh: 这真的很有趣,因为每当我们有入职或客户电话或团队会议时,我们几乎总是有几十个新想法被原型化,但更重要的是,至少有几个几乎不需要干预的可发布 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we talk, stuff comes out, we look at it, we ship it.
zh: 所以我们交谈,东西产出,我们看它,我们发布它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so much fun.
zh: 这太有趣了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Put this back.
zh: 把这个放回去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the next thing I'm gonna mention is that these three things that I've talked to you about
zh: 所以我要提到的下一件事是,我跟你谈到的这三件事

speaker: Unknown
en: Really rely on having your workflow, your code base, your project set up to work in an isolated cloud environment.
zh: 真的依赖于把你的工作流、你的代码库、你的项目设置为在隔离的云环境中工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that way the agents aren't trapped on an individual's machine.
zh: 这样智能体就不会被困在个人的机器上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's several reasons why this is important.
zh: 所以这之所以重要有几个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first one is to eliminate what some people are calling lid anxiety.
zh: 所以第一个是消除一些人所说的盖子焦虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: You wanna be able to close your laptop.
zh: 你希望能够合上你的笔记本电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've probably seen people running around the conference with their laptops open while stuff is working, or at the airport, or there's some posts on Twitter or whatever about people having their laptop tethered to their phone in their car as they're driving home.
zh: 你可能看到过人们在会议上跑来跑去,他们的笔记本电脑开着,同时在处理事情,或者在机场,或者 Twitter 上有一些帖子,关于人们把笔记本电脑绑定到车上,开车回家。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was actually probably the impetus for me and for a few people on our team to even start working on this.
zh: 这实际上可能是我和我们团队中的几个人开始做这个的动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Last year, I started working with Claude Code a lot.
zh: 去年,我开始大量使用 Claude Code。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a, I think at the time, six-month-old.
zh: 我有一个,我想当时,六个月大的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't want to be tied to my laptop or have that stress.
zh: 我不想被束缚在笔记本电脑上或拥有那种压力。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Things are working always.
zh: 事情总是在运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It eliminated that problem for us that people have been talking about for the past year.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Their laptops, unless you have impeccable hygiene, probably have a bunch of stuff on it that you don't want the LLMs or editors to have access to.
zh: 他们的笔记本电脑,除非你有无可挑剔的卫生习惯,可能上面有一堆你不希望 LLM 或编辑器访问的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, everybody's working on these sandboxes and approval flows, but really, you're in one of two camps.

speaker: Unknown
en: You're either approving a bunch of stuff or you're hoping that your auto-approval flow or your YOLO mode or whatever is configured properly and your sandbox is configured properly and doesn't read a bunch of stuff on your laptop that it should have.
zh: 你要么是在批准一堆东西,要么你是希望你的自动审批流程或你的 YOLO 模式或任何东西配置正确,并且你的沙箱配置正确,不会读取你笔记本电脑上的一堆它不该读的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as the previous talk mentioned, these agents are getting more autonomous.
zh: 正如之前的演讲所提到的,这些智能体正在变得更加自主。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're getting really resourceful.
zh: 它们变得真的足智多谋。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're trying to please you and do what you said.
zh: 它们试图取悦你并做你说的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you say, hey, wipe the staging database and it finds a token on your laptop that it can use and it thinks it's working with staging, but actually it's production and now it just deleted everything.
zh: 所以当你说,嘿,清除暂存数据库,而它在你的笔记本电脑上发现了一个它可以使用的令牌,并且它认为它正在与暂存一起工作,但实际上它是生产环境,现在它刚刚删除了一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not trying to say this is happening constantly, but it still happens.
zh: 我并不是说这一直在发生,但它仍然会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for us, the peace of mind of just letting anybody run with these experiments and ideas and prototypes and real code,
zh: 而对我们来说,让任何人都能自由地进行这些实验、想法、原型和真正的代码,

speaker: Unknown
en: Without having to worry about this is really worthwhile.
zh: 而不必担心这一点,真的非常值得。

speaker: Unknown
en: To go one step further on that, it's not just, hey, make sure they don't have the credentials that they shouldn't have.
zh: 在那一点上更进一步，不仅仅是，嘿，确保他们没有他们不该有的凭证。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also make sure they can't exfiltrate your code or your projects or your secrets or your content to somewhere they shouldn't be able to.
zh: 还要确保他们无法把你的代码、项目、密钥或内容泄露到他们不该能到达的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have a configurable network sandbox and you say, look, these are the places you're allowed to access.
zh: 所以你有一个可配置的网络沙箱，你说，看，这些是你被允许访问的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are the ones you can't access.
zh: 这些是你不能访问的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And any time it tries to access something that it shouldn't, it just pops up and says, hey, I tried to access something.
zh: 每当它试图访问它不该访问的东西时，它就会弹出来并说，嘿，我试图访问某个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to give it access?
zh: 你想给它访问权限吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you're trying to integrate a new vendor and need documentation.
zh: 也许你正试图集成一个新的供应商并且需要文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can do it on a per-ticket basis for the whole project.
zh: 你可以在整个项目的基础上按工单（ticket）来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so again, that peace of mind of people can do things.
zh: 所以同样，那种人们可以做事情的心安感。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they need new access, it's easy to grant it.
zh: 如果他们需要新的访问权限，很容易授予。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're not going to leak a bunch of important data by running agents in YOLO mode.
zh: 我们不会通过以 YOLO 模式运行智能体而泄露一堆重要数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the last thing I'll mention about that is that this is the key for allowing your non-technical team members to trigger real work, right?
zh: 关于这一点我要提到的最后一件事是，这是允许你的非技术团队成员触发真正工作的关键，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Non-technical people don't have development environments set up on their computers.
zh: 非技术人员没有在他们的电脑上设置开发环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we've gotten our support people, our growth people, to actually be meaningfully impacting the product by just talking to users, seeing bugs, experiencing themselves, and just go to Slack or the app itself and say, hey, fix this.
zh: 但我们已经让我们的支持人员、我们的增长人员，实际上通过仅仅与用户交谈、发现 bug、亲身体验，然后去 Slack 或应用程序本身并说，嘿，修复这个，从而对产品产生有意义的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: They fix it, screenshots are shown, engineer gets it, gets merged.
zh: 他们修复了它，显示了截图，工程师收到了它，被合并了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Without that, they'd have to put it in linear and the engineer would eventually pick it up and a PM would triage it or whatever.
zh: 没有那个的话，他们必须把它放进 linear，工程师最终会接手它，一个 PM 会对其进行分类或其他什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: None of that here, you just ask for it and it's done.
zh: 这里都没有这些，你只要请求它，它就完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now the reason people didn't do this up until somewhat recently, this was really painful.
zh: 现在人们直到最近才这样做的原因是，这真的很痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Getting your full thing set up in this kind of sandbox environment used to be really, really painful.
zh: 在这种沙箱环境中把你的整个东西设置好以前真的、真的很痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the agents have gotten better.
zh: 但智能体已经变得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have our own environment setup assistant that kind of takes your project and gets it to work in one of these sandboxes.
zh: 我们有自己的环境设置助手，它基本上拿走你的项目并让它在这些沙箱中的一个里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But honestly, whether you use us or not, I highly recommend you get your project working this way, and you can just get Claude Code or Codex to do this for you.
zh: 但老实说，无论你是否使用我们，我强烈你让你的项目以这种方式工作，你可以直接让 Claude Code 或 Codex 为你做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to use us, but we think it's the best way.
zh: 你不必使用我们，但我们认为这是最好的方式。

en: And the last lesson is to benchmark agents on your code base.
zh: 而最后一个教训是在你的代码库上对智能体进行基准测试。

zh: 所以我们这样做的方式是我们选择代表伟大工程工作的拉取请求。

zh: 你选择你想使用和基准测试的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you get a quality versus cost and time breakdown in your code base.
zh: 然后你在你的代码库中获得一个质量与成本和时间的细分。

en: Now, why do you want to do this?
zh: 现在，你为什么想做这个？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 有很多原因，但其中一个是如果你有点偏离公共基准，SweeBench 或 TerminalBench 或其他东西，那些任务可能完全与你的任务无关。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, SweeBench is all in Python, we're Ruby on Rails.
zh: 比如，SweeBench 全是 Python，我们是 Ruby on Rails。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not the case that the benchmarks are identical for them.
zh: 基准测试对它们来说是一样的并不是这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's trends that do compare, but the results can be very, very different.
zh: 有确实进行比较的趋势，但结果可能非常、非常不同。

en: And I'm gonna swap over to my browser one more time here.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: This one here is quality versus cost.
zh: 这个是质量与成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: This one here is quality versus time.
zh: 这个是质量与时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll start with this one.
zh: 我从这个开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see some trends here.
zh: 你可以在这里看到一些趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see that the Anthropic,
zh: 你可以看到那个 Anthropic，

speaker: Unknown

en: This is for our code base again.
zh: 这又是针对我们的代码库。

zh: 我不是试图在这里做任何一般的声明。

en: By cost, the Anthropic stuff is clearly just so much more expensive for us.
zh: 按成本，Anthropic 的东西对我们来说显然只是贵得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the Codex stuff has been cheaper for us.
zh: Codex 的东西对我们来说更便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this causes a change of behavior.
zh: 所以这导致了行为的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still use the different models.
zh: 我们仍然使用不同的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's different use cases for them.
zh: 它们有不同的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: We like the variety.
zh: 我们喜欢这种多样性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still use all these things.

speaker: Unknown
en: But when we saw these results, they kind of matched our vibe check.
zh: 但当我们看到这些结果时，它们有点符合我们的氛围检查。

en: We wanted to kind of have hard data, too.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of switched our default to that for the few days we had it, and then it went away and switched back to Codex.

speaker: Unknown
en: But the most important thing is because we're agnostic, none of that had any meaningful disruption on our work.
zh: 但最重要的是，因为我们是不可知论的，所有这些都没有对我们的工作造成任何有意义的破坏。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were able to just kind of switch back and forth really easily.
zh: 我们能够非常轻松地来回切换。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以这对我们来说基本上变成了 100%，比如我们 99.9% 的拉取请求是由智能体大量生成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know that quality and reliability and security are really important, so we still have humans look at everything.
zh: 我们知道质量和可靠性及安全性真的很重要，所以我们仍然有人类查看所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have agents help with it all, but everything's human-reviewed.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你知道，对于我们相对较小的团队，我们在过去一个月有 105 亿个 token，你可以稍微看看我们关于 Claude 在这里所说的。

speaker: Unknown

en: And Codex had four times as many sessions, and it was cheaper overall.

zh: 所以同样，我们目前绝大部分工作是通过 Codex 合并的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still use the other models.
zh: 我们仍然使用其他模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: More and more is happening through GLM 5.2.
zh: 越来越多的事情正在通过 GLM 5.2 发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gonna invest in that.
zh: 将对其进行投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing that we're really excited to do going forward with this benchmarking is automatically, like you've probably heard about people routing tasks to the right models and all that, but how does some third party know what to route for your code base?
zh: 关于这个基准测试，未来我们真的很兴奋去做的一件事是自动地，就像你可能听说过人们把任务路由到正确的模型等等，但是第三方怎么知道为你的代码库路由什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a way that you know what's gonna work best for which task for your project.
zh: 这是一种你知道什么最适合你的项目的哪个任务的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're going to look at automatically routing that for you.
zh: 我们将研究为你自动路由那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to leave you with a few recommendations.
zh: 所以我要给你们留下几点建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first, get your code base and agents working in a sandbox.
zh: 首先，让你的代码库和智能体在沙箱中工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It unlocks a lot of different things, a lot of different workflows, everything I've talked about and more.
zh: 它解锁了许多不同的东西，许多不同的工作流，我谈论的所有事情以及更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second, integrate agents into the relevant human interfaces so your team and your agents can work together and don't have to context switch and copy context back and forth.
zh: 其次，将智能体集成到相关的人类界面中，这样你的团队和你的智能体可以一起工作，不必进行上下文切换并来回复制上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, we think SuperNectar is the best way to do it, but plenty of people are home-rolling things, packing things together, figuring out how to make this happen, because if not, the friction is just really high.
zh: 显然，我们认为 SuperNectar 是最好的方式，但很多人正在自己打造东西，把东西打包在一起，弄清楚如何实现这一点，因为如果不这样，摩擦真的很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And lastly, find a way to benchmark and become model agnostic, so you're not tied to anybody and you can just constantly stay at that right part on the frontier of cost, speed, quality.
zh: 最后，找到一种方法来进行基准测试并成为模型不可知论的，这样你就不会受制于任何人，你可以不断地保持在成本、速度、质量前沿的正确位置。

speaker: Unknown
